How widespread this phenomenon actually was in practice is difficult to say. candidates.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
candidates.raw_excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images. NASA called the asteroid the "Great Pumpkin," while others called it the "Halloween Asteroid." (Image credit: NAIC-Arecibo/NSF) Why it mattered Be afraid, be very afraid... Okay, not really, but there is reason to be concerned about near-Earth objects and the time in which they are detected. "According to the catalog of near-Earth objects (NEOs) kept by the Minor Planet Center, this is the closest currently known approach by an object this large until asteroid 1999 AN10, at about 2,600 feet (800 meters) in size, approaches at about 1 lunar distance (238,000 miles from Earth) in August 2027," NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) reported in 2015. NASA’s Near-Earth Object Observations Program, sometimes called “Spaceguard,” works to catalog these type of objects and predicts some of their paths if they could be potentially threats to our planet. While there are no known credible impact threats to date, it doesn't mean the "Great Pumpkin," or rather a great impactor, isn't real. candidates.title: Betelgeuse is haunted by a cosmic poltergeist tormenting the doomed star's atmosphere
candidates.raw_excerpt: Something spooky is stirring in the shadows of the infamous star Betelgeuse, a cosmic poltergeist that is disrupting the atmosphere of the red supergiant. New radio observations have shown Betelgeuse's smaller stellar companion, Siwarha (not Betelguese Betelguese, unfortunately), cutting through the supergiant's extended atmosphere and leaving a wake in its path, like a jet boat slicing through a lake. Because the name of this red supergiant star located about 650 light-years away from Earth, marking the shoulder of constellation Orion, is Betelgeuse, which means "the hand of al-Jawza" in Arabic, the companion was named Siwarha , meaning "her bracelet." "This companion is orbiting so close to the star that it actually passes through its extended atmosphere," Lynn Matthews, the principal research scientist at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Haystack Observatory who led the new observations, said in a statement . candidates.title: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California (video)
candidates.raw_excerpt: SpaceX celebrated Halloween with an early-morning launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO). The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base just after midnight ET on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093. The record for a SpaceX first stage is 37 , set this past August by the booster B1067. The Falcon 9's upper stage did its job as well today, deploying the 27 Starlink satellites into LEO about 62 minutes after launch. They're joining more than 11,000 spacecraft in the Starlink megaconstellation, which is by far the largest satellite network ever assembled. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship shortly after launch on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1093 launches SDA-T1TL-B | SDA-T1TL-C | Transporter-16 | 14 Starlink missions Today's launch was the 118th Falcon 9 flight of 2026 so far. More than 70% of these missions have been devoted to building out the Starlink network. SpaceX has also launched its Falcon Heavy and Starship rockets three times apiece this year. Falcon Heavy is an operational vehicle, but Starship remains in the test-flight phase. The company is currently gearing up for another Starship launch , which is expected to take place sometime in November.

candidates.raw_excerpt:
China's first shipborne stealth reconnaissance-strike integrated drone GJ-21 has recently completed its first takeoff and landing operation aboard the Sichuan, China's first Type 076 amphibious assault ship, a navy source said.

This represents another breakthrough made by China in the development of amphibious assault ships and marks that the Chinese Navy has acquired the capability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms, the navy source noted.

The Sichuan, hull number 51, is the first Type 076 amphibious assault ship designed and built independently by China. It was launched on December 27, 2024, and is named after southwest China's Sichuan Province.

The Sichuan has a full-load displacement of over 40,000 tonnes and features a dual-island superstructure along with a full-length flight deck.

The vessel features the innovative application of automated landing guidance system, integrated electric power system, and electromagnetic catapult and arrestor technologies. It is designed to carry fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles, helicopters and amphibious equipment.

Since beginning its first sea trials in November 2025, the Sichuan has steadily conducted various maritime tests as planned, successfully completing the debugging of various equipment and overall operational stability testing, the source said.

Twelve of those 14 liftoffs have been successful. The GSLV Mark II debuted in 2010, the same year its predecessor retired. That previous launchers, the Mark I, flew a total of six times, with two failures. NVS-03 was the fourth Indian launch of 2026 and the third operated by ISRO. candidates.title: Government Spending on Civil Space Topped $42 Billion in FY2026
candidates.raw_excerpt: Government spending on civil space activities is more than just NASA. A new Aerospace Corporation report details the $42.6 billion allocated for civil space in FY2026 and compares it to FY2025 and the still-pending request for FY2027. NASA is the largest share, but only 55 percent of the total. Overall, the report characterizes the civil space budget as going through tumultuous times with the White House and Congress out of sync and the FY2027 outcome uncertain. The term “civil space” immediately evokes NASA, NOAA and perhaps the Office of Science at the Department of Energy (DOE), but Aerospace’s Lindsay DeMarchi painstakingly scoured all non-defense agencies and identified a total of 19 that are allocated money to “support, enable, or leverage space through direct and indirect means.” In terms of spending, the DOE is highest after NASA at 18 percent, with the others ranging from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at 6.79 percent down to the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) at 0.05 percent. Source: The Aerospace Corporation’s Center for Space Policy and Strategy. DeMarchi then categorizes them into seven “national priorities” — American Leadership and Manufacturing; Fundamental Science; Infrastructure, Energy and Resiliency; Remote Sensing Applications; Homeland Security; Streamlining and Expansion; and Workforce Development. Source: The Aerospace Corporation’s Center for Space Policy and Strategy. The report compares FY2025 and FY2026, where funding is finalized, and the FY2027 request. The bottom line, not surprisingly, is that the budget for space across civil government “is experiencing a period of significant uncertainty.” FY2026 encompassed the longest government shutdown in history, but Congress ultimately appropriated much more than the President’s Budget Request (PBR) and added billions more in a separate reconciliation bill — the One Big, Beautiful Bill Act, OBBBA (also called the Working Families Tax Cut Act, WFTC)

candidates.title: The Taurid meteor shower isn't much to look at. That's why I love it
candidates.raw_excerpt: I used to make a basic mistake with meteor showers — I treated the zenith hourly rate (ZHR) like a timetable. If a shower were advertised at 20 meteors per hour, I'd go outside expecting something roughly every three minutes. After 10 quiet minutes, I'd start wondering what I was doing wrong. After half an hour, I'd start to doubt the whole idea of meteor showers . The Northern and Southern Taurids cured me of all that. Two linked meteor showers that peak around Nov. 4-5 and Nov. 11-12 this year, they each manage only about five meteors per hour under ideal conditions. In reality, you may see fewer. You may spend a long time seeing none. So what's the point? I've come to regard their paucity of "shooting stars" as a feature, not a flaw, for the Taurids have taught me to stop counting meteors and instead just observe the sky. I go outside for Taurus, the Pleiades, Auriga, and whatever else happens to be visible. If a Taurid crosses the sky, excellent. If not, the evening hasn't failed. The reason is that they are also known for occasionally producing very bright meteors, or fireballs — although "occasionally" is important. Don't go outside expecting a procession of them. What's happening and when to look The Taurid meteor showers remind us to get outside and watch the stars of winter rise into the night sky. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) The Taurids hit Earth's atmosphere at about 18 miles (29 kilometers) per second. That's relatively slow for a meteor shower. It's one reason Taurids can be more memorable than meteors from faster showers. In his letter to the University of Kentucky’s Office of Equal Opportunity requesting the exemption, Durman wrote that “substituting automated machine processing for human presence, authentic listening, and personal responsibility in my work directly conflicts with my obligation to uphold human dignity and flourishing as primary.” Humanism isn’t an organized religion, but does qualify as a religion under federal statutes.
